architecture_rules: Screen -> Engine -> Validator -> Model -> PostgreSQL. Never break this order.
SQL only inside Models. Business logic only inside Engines. Validation only inside Validators. UI only inside Screens.
Soft-delete only, no physical DELETE FROM in application code.
BS-first audit trail: every audit timestamp stores both AD (authoritative) and BS (display) via the centralized Date Engine.
No hardcoded values - configurable via the settings table/engine where applicable.
No duplicate logic - reuse existing Engines/Models (e.g. SimpleMasterEngine for generic lookup masters).

domain_glossary.meaning: Bikram Sambat date - the PRIMARY business calendar in this project.
Anno Domini date - secondary, used for DB storage/sorting/calculations.

domain_glossary.term: CC / Customs Charge / CC on Free Goods
domain_glossary.meaning: A CUSTOMS DUTY calculated on the Free Quantity of a purchase line, using a country's custom_percent (see country_tax table/engine) applied to a declared customs value per unit. This is an IMPORT/CUSTOMS concept, NOT inventory costing. Do NOT confuse with weighted-average cost per unit (a separate, unrelated calculation for inventory valuation).
Maximum Retail Price - statutory ceiling price for sale, set by manufacturer.
Final per-unit cost after Purchase Rate + Freight + CC + other charges are added. It is an OUTPUT of these charges, never an INPUT/basis for calculating any of them - avoid circular references.
The only place stock quantity/expiry lives in this project. There is no stock column on `item` itself. Total stock = SUM(item_batch.batch_qty).

domain_glossary.term: Landing Cost basis vs Purchase Rate for free goods
domain_glossary.meaning: Free Qty always has Purchase Rate = 0 by definition. Never use Purchase Rate as a basis for any charge calculation on free goods - it will always compute to zero.
